rubrics.criterion: The field-usage rule's blast-radius analytics (unioned modules, distinct areas, and entry-point membership over the modules reaching each selected field) is obtained from the module-graph class (packages/cli-utils/src/commands/scan/module-graph.ts), and the rule's collection step no longer folds the graph's dependents closure, per-module areas, and entry-point membership into its own local accumulators.
rubrics.rationale: The envy in this rule is a per-set reverse-closure fold over the owner's data; resolving it means the reach computation is hosted by the class that owns the import map, whose reach API already computes the same union. This is the core Move-Method outcome for the field-usage manifestation, and it can be satisfied by the existing reach method or by a new batch-shaped owner method.

rubrics.criterion: The fetch-depth rule places each query by asking the module-graph class for the entry-point distance of its defining module (via the existing per-module distance method or a new owner method), with no rule-side entry-distance table built by walking the graph's entry points and raw import edges; per-query area labels likewise come from the graph class.
rubrics.rationale: This manifestation re-implements the owner's memoised distance walk with local frontier state; the semantic outcome is that the walk lives on the graph class again and the rule only consumes a distance per query, however the owner chooses to batch it.

rubrics.criterion: The cross-feature-fragments rule resolves module areas through the module-graph class at the points of use (spread-site labelling in the visitor, defining-area labelling in the collection fold), and the eager rule-local module-to-area index built from the graph's import map in the rule's setup step no longer exists.
rubrics.rationale: This manifestation is an eager copy of the owner's raw edge data consumed via closure; resolving it means the rule asks the owner for an area where it needs one instead of maintaining a derived index, so all three phases (setup, visitor, collection) stop consulting rule-local graph data.

rubrics.criterion: The graph analytics implementations were not merely relocated to another non-owner location: scan-context methods, standalone helper functions, or a newly introduced intermediate object still carry the reach/distance/area computations (graph-walk or fold logic) outside the module-graph class.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible dodgy repair routes the rules through the scan context facade or a new helper module so that rule functions look thin while the analytics implementation stays outside the class that owns the data; this leaves the misplaced responsibility intact and must be detectable as a failure.

rubrics.criterion: Every consumer call site of the moved analytics goes through the module-graph class after the change, and type/import declarations that existed only to support the inlined implementations are removed (e.g. a RuleDatapoint type import added to a rule that no longer declares a local datapoint array).
rubrics.rationale: The diffusion includes small supporting edits (a type import needed only by the inline-collect rewrite); a complete change updates every call site and leaves no imports whose only purpose was the inlined code.

rubrics.criterion: Any newly added module-graph member that serves the rules' set- or batch-shaped needs fits the class's existing API style and reuses its memoised state (entry-point set, reverse closure, distance map) rather than recomputing graph state independently per caller.
rubrics.rationale: The owner class memoises entry points, reverse closures and distances by design; a repair that adds owner-side members to serve batch needs should integrate with that existing memoised state, otherwise it trades consumer-side duplication for owner-side duplication.

rubrics.criterion: Dead vestiges of the inlined analytics remain in the rule layer after the repair: a rule-local distance table, module-to-area map, or dependents/areas/entry-points accumulator that is built but no longer used, or a leftover folding/walk loop kept alongside the new owner calls.
rubrics.rationale: Partial repairs often add the owner call while leaving the old inline machinery in place (guarded or unused); tests stay green because outputs come from the new path, so the stale structures only surface as dead code that must be checked by review.

rubrics.criterion: Obsolete artifacts of the temporary inlining linger in the touched rules: an import of a type that is no longer referenced, or a comment that still describes a rule-local distance/area computation that no longer exists.
rubrics.rationale: Stale comments and unused type imports that only made sense while the analytics were inlined mislead the next maintainer about where those computations live, which is exactly the confusion this task is meant to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The scan output changed observable results somewhere: a datapoint's message text, weight, data fields, tie-break or sort order differ from the pre-repair state (for example field-usage ranking by selection count then reach, or fetch-depth ordering by descending distance), so terminal/JSON/graph renderings for the same scanned project are no longer identical.
rubrics.rationale: Two of the three manifestations compute ranking-relevant statistics (blast-radius sizes, entry distances, external-area counts) and were preserved to the byte by the injection; a repair that slightly reorders a sort, re-numbers a weigh, or rewords a message silently changes every consumer of the scan command even though the tests that cover the rules may not pin the exact string.

rubrics.criterion: Queries (or other definitions) with no route from the import-graph entry points are now reported differently or dropped: their reported depth, the wording for an unknown distance, or their position in the result order changed.
rubrics.rationale: The fetch-depth manifestation specifically re-derived the memoised distance walk, including the existence check for unreachable modules; a naive owner-side rewrite (e.g. coercing an unknown distance into a number, or skipping such definitions) produces different statistics exactly where the original behaviour was most subtle.

rubrics.criterion: The repair made collateral edits outside the task's scope: the rule registration table, rule names, datapoint TypeScript interfaces, the scan traversal/context machinery, other scan rules (orphan-fragments, deprecated-usage, operation-complexity, directive usage, input status), or the module-graph class's existing public analytics methods were changed or removed in a way that alters their current behaviour.
rubrics.rationale: The misplaced analytics live in three rules while the rest of the pipeline is a shared, stable contract; an over-broad repair that renames the rule objects, re-shapes their datapoint interfaces, or changes existing owner analytics for unrelated callers signals scope bleed and risks breaking alternative consumers the tests do not cover.
